_doc: Endpoints forge intentionally hits that native claude doesn't. The analyzer filters these out of the 'regression' list. Edit when the forge team makes a new product decision about an endpoint divergence. Each entry should explain WHY the divergence is accepted so future maintainers understand. host+path_contains is a substring match.

endpoints_in_alt_not_native.reason: forge polls user OAuth quota for UI usage panel; ~20 hits per session
forge probes npm for latest claude-code package version to show update notifications; 1 hit at session start
forge proactively fetches Anthropic's status page for in-app banners; 1 hit at session start

forge probes npm for the Playwright MCP server package — not visible to Anthropic; user explicitly accepted on 2026-05-28: 'ignore the npmjs, we only care about api that captures data in some form and anthropic has access to it'

Symmetric mirror of the native-only entry below. MCP-server hits depend on which side of the capture happened to have MCP servers attached during the session. Per-session state, not a forge feature divergence — grep confirms zero references in forge source; the claude subprocess itself emits these.

Endpoint emitted by claude CLI 2.1.153 (User-Agent: 'claude-cli/2.1.153 (external, cli)'), not by forge. Grep confirms zero references in forge source. Fires conditionally — only when CLI decides to. Accepted because forge's role is to wrap claude transparently; CLI-emitted endpoints are by definition wire-equivalent.

endpoints_in_native_not_alt_acceptable.reason: Different sessions may have different MCP server lists active depending on trust prompts and per-session config. Native hitting an MCP server ID that alt doesn't (or vice versa) within mcp-proxy is acceptable noise, not a real wire-equivalence failure.
